title: Dispatch: fail-closed ledger closure and true semantic absence (attempt 7)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #477 at 292b716: two P1, one P2, one P3. NO new defect
class, so a FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next — but only if the review
contract is UNCHANGED. Therefore this round implements existing contract
invariants correctly and adds NO new invariant classes. Do not propose contract
changes; if you believe one is needed, report it instead of making it.

ACCEPTED AS FIXED — do not touch: ev::: vs obl::: namespace separation; canonical
semantic facet validation and source/locator binding; registry-wide identity
uniqueness; removal of the five unsupported audit citations; the reviewed
relation table binding audit findings; duplicate projection query rejection
within and across rows.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: CLOSURE IS FAIL-OPEN FOR UNDERIVED EVIDENCE ===
The documentation says evidence-underived blocks closure. Nothing enforces it:
the full-ledger test ACCEPTS that status and explicitly expects five underived
results, and no fail-closed closure predicate exists in this PR at all. As
written, a DIFFERENT set of five unresolved rows would pass identically — the
test pins a count, not an identity.

NOTE A PATTERN: the sibling finding registry (PR #476) shipped the same defect —
a closure predicate that reports readiness without applying the validations
beneath it. Assume fail-open is the default failure mode of any 'ready' helper
and write this one to prove the negative.

FIX:
 * Export a fail-closed closure predicate that returns NOT-READY whenever any
   row carries evidence-underived, and NAMES the exact blocker set.
 * The regression must assert the EXACT blocker identities, not a count. A
   different set of five must FAIL.
 * Test both directions: not-ready on the current ledger with its real blocker
   set, and ready on a fixture where every row is resolved.
 * The committed test that expects five underived results encodes the defect —
   change it deliberately and record why in your notes.

=== P1-B: SOURCE-NEGATIVE EVIDENCE PROVES PHRASE ABSENCE, NOT SEMANTIC ABSENCE ===
The resolver checks selected terms at ONE generated-record path, then searches
only data.executionReadiness.clauses for selected substrings. It never inspects
other structured projection surfaces and cannot recognise an equivalent
representation expressed in different vocabulary. Substring absence is not
semantic absence.

Four anchors also identify the WRONG SOURCE UNIT:
  spell-slot / upcast   -> points at Wizard progression and the terms
                           'spellcastingProgression' and 'slots', not an upcast
                           procedure
  spellbook copying     -> points at the level-gain choice prompt, not the
                           copying time-and-cost clause
  multi-save            -> points at the generic Saving Throws rule, not the
                           audited entries whose later saves were dropped
  half-damage           -> points at the general resistance rule, not the
                           affected creature and hazard success branches
This affects ALL TWELVE source-negative primitives, not only the five currently
reported as underived. Re-audit every one.

FIX, per primitive:
 (a) anchor to the SPECIFIC source unit whose projection is missing;
 (b) search ALL structured projection surfaces, not data.executionReadiness
     alone;
 (c) detect semantically EQUIVALENT representations that use different
     vocabulary — match on semantic shape, not on a chosen substring.
If (c) cannot be established for a primitive, mark it evidence-underived. With
P1-A fixed that correctly BLOCKS closure. Expect the underived set to GROW; that
is the honest outcome and is preferable to a green that means nothing. Do not
tune anchors until exactly five remain.

=== P2-C: ev::: ARITY IS NEVER CHECKED ===
The validator claims four nonempty segments but never checks segment COUNT, so
'ev:::a:::b:::c:::d' passes. FIX: enforce the exact arity for both namespaces
and add negative tests for too few and too many segments.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four
files above. Two sibling dispatches run in parallel on disjoint file sets. Do not
touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any
script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer. Do not modify any
bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or merge. The PR body is
the supervisor's to fix.
acceptance_criteria:
• A fail-closed closure predicate names the exact blocker set and returns not-ready whenever any row is evidence-underived.
• The regression asserts exact blocker identities, not a count; a different set of the same size fails.
• All twelve source-negative primitives anchor to the specific unprojected source unit, search all structured projection surfaces, and detect vocabulary-equivalent representations.
• Primitives whose absence cannot be established are evidence-underived and block closure; the underived set is allowed to grow rather than being tuned to a target size.
• Identity arity is enforced for both namespaces with too-few and too-many negative tests.
• The review contract is unchanged, so a fix-verification review remains permissible.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
